title: A cubic counterexample to edge-pattern convex domination
scope: Pirot-Sereni (arXiv:1904.05618; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 35(4) (2021) 2815-2843) Conjecture 2, also Conjecture 1.5.1 of Pirot's 2019 thesis, is false at d = 3, r = 2. The 8-vertex edge-rooted pattern P (root edge 01; edges 01,02,03,15,17,34,46,56: a 6-cycle with two pendants) is 3-regular, of exact depth 2 and girth 6, with e(P) = (2/5,14/5,4/5). With alpha = (1/1000,7/27,1/3), alpha.e(P) = 67027/67500 < 1, while every acyclic 3-regular depth-2 edge-rooted pattern (all 81 leaf-count forms) has alpha.e(T) >= 3001/3000. So no convex combination of tree constraints is weaker than e(P). The source's optimized bounds (Lemma 10) are unaffected.
source_targets: F. Pirot, J.-S. Sereni, arXiv:1904.05618 v1/v6 Conjecture 2; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 35(4) 2021
substantive_reason: Refutes a human-posed structural conjecture from a SIAM J. Discrete Math. paper and the first author's thesis, under its exact hypotheses: an explicit girth-6 pattern defeats every convex combination of tree constraints. It is not a domain correction, and the source's own optimized-vector computations do not contradict it.
